signature: @Blob field (processor, exeris-codegen-java): EXT-PROC-1031 on a GLOBAL entity, EXT-PROC-1032 on a non-BlobRef field; the field is no column and leaves the create and update bodies; + PUT/GET/HEAD/DELETE {base}/{id}/blobs/{field}; + 'storage' in the required subsystems
justification: A @Blob field was emitted as an ordinary column and nothing stored its bytes. It is now served on its own routes through the kernel blob store, so it stops being a column and a request-body member, and an application with one requires a store at boot. A consumer that read or wrote the field as a column moves to the field's routes; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-18-blob-extracted.md and java-19-blob-field-routes.md carry the steps.

signature: @ExerisDomain entity (processor): EXT-PROC-1033 when its package does not end in .domain; EXT-PROC-1034 per JavaBean accessor the generated application calls and the entity lacks (Lombok @Getter/@Setter/@Data/@Value count); + -Aexeris.metadataOnly=true skips both
justification: The generated kernel application places its infrastructure beside a .domain package and binds entity state through accessors. Without either, generation threw an exception after a partial write or the generated code failed in javac. Both are now stable build-time refusals on the source element. A build that only produces metadata for something other than kernel generation sets -Aexeris.metadataOnly=true; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-21-entity-layout-and-accessors-refused.md carries the steps.

signature: <Entity>GraphSync (exeris-codegen-java): syncToGraph reads the stored targets of each relation type in one outgoing traverseBreadthFirst hop, deletes those the entity no longer holds and upserts the held ones; + List<UUID> @GraphEdge, one edge per distinct key; EXT-GEN-3003 on a @GraphEdge field that is neither UUID nor List<UUID>
justification: The graph sync only upserted, so an updated or cleared edge field left the edge to the old target in place, and a collection edge emitted a single upsert that did not compile. Each edge is now synchronised against what the graph stores, a collection edge holds its targets' UUID keys as a scalar edge does, and a List of entities on a @GraphEdge is refused before any write with the List<UUID> to hold instead. docs/migration/0.11.0/java-24-graph-collection-edges.md carries the steps.

signature: V{tier}{nnnnnn}__create_{table}.sql (exeris-codegen-java): a field in a system role whose @ExerisDomain flag is off (tenant, audited, softDelete, versioned) is declared as a domain column from its type; the system columns of an active role are unchanged
justification: The create-table migration left out every field named or marked for a system role, whatever the entity's flags, while the repository read and wrote such a field as an ordinary column when the role's flag was off, so its first query named a column the table did not have. Both now take the active roles from one place. The regenerated migration of an affected entity differs from one a database has applied; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-25-system-marker-without-flag-is-a-column.md carries the steps.

signature: <Entity>Handler.<Action>Request (exeris-codegen-java): a body component whose @ActionParam declares defaultValue is declared with its boxed type, and a compact constructor sets the default when it is null
justification: The defaultValue of a body-bound action parameter was read by nothing, so an omitted member reached the entity method as 0, false or null, while the same attribute on a query parameter was applied. The record applies it, and the boxed component keeps an omitted value apart from an explicit zero. A caller that relied on the zero value sends it, and code that names the record sees the boxed accessor type; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-28-action-body-param-default.md carries the steps.

signature: <Entity>CreateDto / <Entity>UpdateDto, list sort keys and filters, <Entity>Repository.update (exeris-codegen-java) and <Entity>Create / <Entity>Update / <Entity>SortField / <Entity>Filter (exeris-codegen-ts): a field in a system role whose @ExerisDomain flag is off (tenant, audited, softDelete, versioned) is carried by both request bodies, sortable and filterable by its @Field, and written by every update; the fields of an active role are unchanged
justification: The API treated every name a systemFields block declared as server-owned whatever the entity's flags, while the migration and the repository treat a role whose flag is off as an ordinary column. Such a field was out of both bodies and the update never wrote it, so nothing could set the column. The API now takes the active roles from the same place, on the Java and the TypeScript side. A client that relied on the server dropping the field now has its value stored; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-26-system-marker-without-flag-is-client-writable.md and ts-15-system-marker-without-flag-in-request-types.md carry the steps.

signature: V{tier}{nnnnnn}__create_{table}.sql, V3000000__foreign_keys.sql, {E}Repository, {E}Handler, OpenAPI (exeris-codegen-java): a ONE_TO_MANY List<Target> with mappedBy holds no column and reads as null; its cascadeDelete sets ON DELETE CASCADE on the owning foreign key; any other List of entities is refused with EXT-GEN-3003
justification: An inverse collection was stored as a JSON column of the owner's table, a copy that no constraint, tenant scope or write of the target kept in step, and its cascadeDelete reached no constraint. Its rows are now the target's rows: no column, index, bind or read; the handler resets it to null after decoding; OpenAPI marks it readOnly and names the child list route its rows are read from; the processor requires its setter only (EXT-PROC-1034). A List of entities that no mappedBy ties to a key of the target is refused before any write. docs/migration/0.11.0/java-29-inverse-collection-holds-no-column.md carries the steps.

signature: <Entity>Service (exeris-codegen-java): <Entity>Service(<Entity>Repository) -> <Entity>Service(<Entity>Repository, <Entity>GraphSync) for a @Graph entity that is not TENANT or UNIVERSE, whose save/update/updateFromRequest call syncToGraph and delete calls deleteFromGraph after the repository returns; + RuntimeComponents.create<Entity>GraphSync()/<entity>GraphSync() for every @Graph entity; + GraphKernelProviders.GRAPH_ENGINE in COMPOSITION_SCOPES; + <Entity>GraphSync.registerDescriptors(), called first by RuntimeLifecycle.run()
justification: The generated graph sync was built, registered and called by nothing, so a booted application's graph stayed empty and, on the Community SQL graph, had no tables. The service is the one seam every generated write passes through, so it now projects each write after the repository returns, and the composition root builds the graph sync and registers its descriptors at boot (ADR-070 Amendment 4). A consumer subclass or override that constructed the service with its repository alone passes the graph sync as well, and a graph failure now fails the write route; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-30-graph-sync-wired.md carries the steps.

signature: V{tier}{nnnnnn}__create_{table}.sql (exeris-codegen-java): a List<X> field is declared TEXT instead of VARCHAR(255)
justification: A List field is stored as one JSON text value, and a VARCHAR(255) column held a List<UUID> of at most six keys. The column now has no declared width. The regenerated migration of an entity with a List field differs from one a database has applied; docs/migration/0.11.0/java-33-list-columns-are-text.md carries the steps.

signature: <Entity>ListQuery (exeris-codegen-java): + String search (last component), + SEARCHABLE, + MAX_SEARCH_LENGTH, five-component constructor kept; GET {base}: 'search' reserved, so a field named search is no longer a filter; + search query parameter, 400 when longer than 100 characters or non-blank on an entity with nothing searchable; OpenAPI list operation + search when searchable
justification: ADR-096 Amendment 4: the list route matches one case-insensitive term as a substring against the String fields @Field(searchable) marks, and every String field without @Field. A record pattern or deconstruction of <Entity>ListQuery breaks on the sixth component, while code calling the five-component constructor compiles unchanged. A field named search, which was an equality filter, is no longer one. docs/migration/0.11.0/java-31-list-route-search.md carries the steps.
